paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea, and I'm leaning in so close my mustache is in the dough. Jesus says, "anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it." (Luke 18:17) A baby doesn't bring a résumé. A baby doesn't hand over a list of everything it's done right. It just comes with open hands, and that's how the kingdom is received.

Now look at the ruler, because he's the other side of the coin. He says, "All these I have kept from my youth," and then Jesus tells him he still lacks one thing. (Luke 18:21-22) The ruler became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy. (Luke 18:23) I think what he was holding onto was heavy, and Jesus wanted him to have both hands free to follow Him. So here's the question for you, baker: what are YOU holding so tight that you can't hold out your hands?

And when the people ask, "Who then can be saved?" Jesus says, "What is impossible with man is possible with God." (Luke 18:26-27) Nobody climbs in by being good enough, rich enough or tidy enough, because no one is good except God alone. (Luke 18:19) Peter says they left all they had to follow Jesus, and Jesus promises "many times more in this age" and "in the age to come, eternal life." (Luke 18:28-30) Friend, that's the best deal in the whole bakery: come with empty hands, and God fills them.
